Case study 6: Pepsi marketing strategy gone wrong

Rewriting Legal History: The Pepsi Jet Saga ✈️

In 1996, Pepsi launched a commercial offering a Harrier jet as a sweepstakes prize. Little did they know, college student John Leonard took the joke seriously. He amassed a whopping 7 million Pepsi Points, the jet’s supposed equivalent, and sent his points along with a check to claim his prize.

Pepsi, however, denied Leonard his dream, arguing that the commercial was merely humorous and the Harrier jet wasn’t even listed in their catalog. A legal battle ensued, forever etching the case of Leonard v. PepsiCo, Inc. in contract law history.

Against all odds, the court ruled in favor of Leonard. They deemed that Pepsi’s offer was genuine and that Leonard had rightfully accepted it. The court couldn’t dismiss the fact that Leonard had no way of discerning the joke.

This landmark victory marked a turning point for both Leonard and Pepsi. The beverage giant reluctantly paid Leonard $792,000 in damages, while also revising its marketing strategies. Gone were the days of whimsical sweepstakes prizes; Pepsi adopted a more cautious tone in their advertising, respecting the fine print. 🍿✨
